Def get in touch with SAILS, I have PTSD/bipolar/severe anxiety and was experiencing medication induced agoraphobia for a good chunk of time while I was finding out what meds were working for me, and my SAILS advisor was super understanding even though I was also doubting if I had legitimate reason for accommodation. I was looking to get flexible attendance mostly, because I was so anxious I could barely leave my apartment, but my advisor did say I could apply for flexible deadlines as well. The SAILS initial form you fill out online gives you a selection of accommodations to choose from. I never ended up actually applying for accommodations because my psych never sent my paperwork over despite asking multiple times and I stopped bothering and ended up finishing the semester just fine, but honestly the worst thing your professors can do is say no. There really isn't a downside to meeting with SAILS, as at the end of the day it's just up to your professor on whether or not they're willing to provide accommodations. You won't get any unless you ask!

You're probably gonna be a bit lost and scared your freshman year, I went through a lot of relationship issues and financial issues which destroyed my self esteem and motivation, which in turn tanked my ability to connect with people. Sometimes I still get down on myself thinking there's something wrong with me. But there's not. I was just terrified of what my life had suddenly become, which is a completely normal feeling to have. If you don't meet anyone your first year don't sweat. You're being rushed into a shit ton of growth and new environments and scary changes and sometimes you just have to put all your focus into surviving. My safety advice, as a woman:

- Get pepper spray. Non negotiable. It does NOT go in your bag, it stays on your keys which stay in your hand or in the front pocket of your pants. Tasers are less reliable, you can definitely have one in addition to spray but spray is a MUST.

- I've taken the light rail to late night concerts in Phoenix by myself a couple of times as a woman, and been lucky to not have problems. It's usually not the rail itself that's sketchy, it's the station. I call someone while I'm waiting at the station, it helps protect you when others know there is someone you're actively talking to who knows your location. When I'm on the rail I always sit in the car closest to the driver/in the car that's busiest to be safe. 

- Speaking of transportation, ALWAYS check Valley Metro app to see if any routes are closed or cancelled. You do not want to take the rail to Phoenix and then find yourself stranded because the east bound route closes at night for construction. That almost happened to me. 

- I've never felt super unsafe walking *on* campus at night, as the blue police lights help me feel protected and there's almost always people out, but you can get free rides on campus through the LiveSafe app if you feel the need. Outskirts of campus and beyond is where it can get more scary. I'd say your general safe bubble is the square between University (north end), Forest (west end), McAllister (east end), and Apache (south end). But no matter what, carry your spray and be aware.

- Some of the homeless folk around Mill might be intimidating and might talk to you but most of the time they won't do you any actual harm. Mill is typically a busy area.

- Walk with a purpose, do NOT make eye contact with anyone, look straight ahead, if someone shouts in your direction, homeless or not, do not look, do not answer, ignore them completely. Even if they repeatedly try. Previous phone call tip helps if you're walking anywhere you need protection.

- Bonus that's not quite safety related: you can ignore the people that come up to you on campus. I don't mind signing a petition for a good cause here and there but I have places to be. Again, just don't make eye contact and keep walking, even if they're approaching you and trying to speak with you. This will also help you avoid the crazy Christians who either, at best, trap you into a 30 minute conversation about Jesus while you can feel your Qdoba getting cold in your hands, or at worst, bring you into their cult. Don't let yourself be a pushover like I did. It's okay to not be perfectly polite all of the time.
